title: Vivo X300 Ultra
text:
The Vivo X300 Ultra is a flagship Android-based smartphone developed and manufactured by Vivo. Its camera system was co-engineered with Zeiss. It was announced in China on 30 March 2026 and released there on 3 April as part of the Vivo X300 series. Sales in the first international markets began on 24 April. The highest-specification model in the series, it succeeds the Vivo X200 Ultra and is the first X-series Ultra model to receive an official international release.
The rear camera system consists of 200-megapixel main and periscope telephoto cameras, a 50-megapixel ultrawide camera and a multispectral colour sensor. Each of the three photographic cameras has optical image stabilisation. The main camera uses a 35 mm-equivalent lens, which gives it a narrower field of view than the lenses commonly used for smartphone main cameras. The accessory range includes 200 mm and 400 mm telephoto extenders, a battery grip and a SmallRig video cage.

== History and release ==
Vivo previewed the X300 Ultra at Mobile World Congress in Barcelona on 2 March 2026. The demonstration disclosed its dual 200-megapixel cameras, 400 mm telephoto attachment and SmallRig cage, and confirmed that an Ultra model would be offered outside China for the first time. The formal Chinese launch followed on 30 March. Prices began at CN¥6,999 for the 12 GB RAM and 256 GB storage model and reached CN¥8,999 for a satellite-communication edition with 16 GB of RAM and 1 TB of storage. Retail sales in China began on 3 April.
Vivo announced the international launch on 15 April, with sales in the first overseas markets beginning on 24 April. Distribution covered parts of continental Europe, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America. The United Kingdom and United States were excluded from the official launch plan.
A European model with 16 GB of RAM and 1 TB of storage was listed at €1,999. Spanish online sales began on 24 April, followed by retail availability on 4 May. Vivo released the phone in India on 6 May for ₹159,999 in a 16 GB and 512 GB configuration.

== Design ==
The X300 Ultra has a flat 6.82-inch display, an aluminium frame and a circular rear camera unit. The black version is 8.19 mm (0.322 in) thick and weighs 232 g (8.2 oz). Versions with a glass rear panel are 8.49 mm (0.334 in) thick and weigh 237 g (8.4 oz). Colour names varied by market. The international range comprised Volcano Black, Steppe Green and Alpine White. Indian models were called Eclipse Black and Victory Green. The Chinese range included black, green and silver finishes.
The phone carries IP68 and IP69 ratings under IEC 60529. Vivo's IP68 test covered immersion in 1.5 m (4.9 ft) of fresh water for 30 minutes, and the IP69 test used high-pressure water jets.

== Specifications ==

=== Hardware and display ===
The X300 Ultra uses Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 system on a chip with an Adreno 840 graphics processor. Chinese models were sold with 12 or 16 GB of LPDDR5X memory and 256 GB, 512 GB or 1 TB of UFS 4.1 storage. International configurations have 16 GB of memory and either 512 GB or 1 TB of storage. A 5,800 mm² vapour chamber transfers heat away from the processor and imaging hardware.
Connectivity includes Wi-Fi 7, NFC, infrared and USB 3.2 Gen 2 at up to 10 Gbit/s. International models support an eSIM alongside two nano-SIM slots. An ultrasonic fingerprint reader is built into the display.
The 6.82-inch LTPO AMOLED display has a 3168 × 1440 resolution and an adaptive refresh rate between 1 and 144 Hz. The 144 Hz mode is limited to compatible software. Vivo specifies 4,500 nits as the local peak brightness under a test covering one per cent of the screen. The display supports HDR10+, HDR Vivid and Dolby Vision.
The single-cell silicon-carbon battery has a typical capacity of 6,600 mAh and a rated capacity of 6,395 mAh. It supports 100 W wired and 40 W wireless charging.

=== Cameras ===

The main camera uses a 200-megapixel Sony LYT-901 sensor measuring 1/1.12 inch and a 35 mm-equivalent f/1.85 lens. Its longer focal length produces a tighter standard view than the approximately 24 mm-equivalent lenses found on many other phones. The second 200-megapixel camera pairs a 1/1.4-inch Samsung HP0 sensor with an 85 mm-equivalent periscope lens. Vivo markets this camera as having 3.7× optical zoom. A 50-megapixel Sony LYT-818 sensor with a 14 mm-equivalent lens supplies the ultrawide view. All three lenses use Zeiss T* coatings and optical image stabilisation.
A separate 5-megapixel, 12-channel sensor measures ambient colour and feeds that information into the image-processing system. The VS1+ imaging co-processor handles RAW data before it reaches the main processor. Vivo's camera application provides JPEG, RAW and SuperRAW capture, along with Zeiss portrait simulations and adjustable colour profiles.
The three rear cameras can record 4K video at 120 frames per second with optical stabilisation. The 50-megapixel front camera has autofocus and records 4K video at 60 frames per second. Recording options for the rear system include 10-bit Log using the APV 4:2:2 codec, Dolby Vision, ACES colour management and previewing with a user-supplied three-dimensional lookup table. Rear video modes include 8K at 30 frames per second. Four microphones support directional recording presets intended for speech, concerts and sporting events.
Two Zeiss-branded telephoto extenders attach over the 85 mm camera. The 2.35× version gives a 200 mm-equivalent optical focal length and weighs 153 g (5.4 oz). The 4.7× version gives a 400 mm-equivalent focal length and weighs 248 g (8.7 oz). Vivo offered the lenses separately and as part of a Photographer Kit with an imaging grip. The grip adds physical controls, a tripod socket and a 2,300 mAh battery. A video cage developed with SmallRig provides mounting points for handles, microphones, lights and a cooling fan.

=== Software ===
The phone shipped with Android 16 and OriginOS 6. The X300 and X300 Pro had introduced OriginOS internationally in October 2025, replacing Funtouch OS on Vivo's global flagship models.
International X300 Ultra models include Google Mobile Services and the Google Play store. Vivo promised five major operating-system upgrades and seven years of security maintenance. OriginOS supports cross-device file transfer with iPhones, iPads and Windows or macOS computers.

== Reception ==
The camera system received favourable reviews. Android Central placed the X300 Ultra at the top of the camera phones it had tested in 2026, citing image consistency among the three rear cameras and the expanded video modes. PetaPixel found the focal lengths, RAW controls and colour adjustments useful for different styles of photography. Its reviewer initially encountered uneven dynamic range and colour. Two firmware updates improved those areas during the review period. Digital Camera World praised stabilisation, manual video controls and output from each rear camera. The size of the camera housing and the amount of preinstalled software reduced its assessment.
DXOMARK gave the camera an overall score of 170, ranking it third in the site's global smartphone camera table on 1 June 2026. Its photo and video scores were 174 and 162. The laboratory noted accurate portraits and strong detail from the ultrawide and telephoto cameras, with occasional autofocus errors, noise and unnatural textures in difficult low-light scenes. In a direct comparison with the Oppo Find X9 Ultra, Engadget preferred Vivo's ultrawide camera and video stabilisation. The publication regarded Oppo's built-in 10× camera as a more flexible arrangement for long-range still photography.
The telephoto attachments drew qualified praise. TechRadar found that the two extenders added useful reach for travel and street photography and produced images that remained usable at their stated focal lengths. Android Authority obtained detailed photographs at 400 mm and 800 mm with the larger extender. Its practical limitations included a minimum focusing distance of roughly four to five metres, a top-heavy grip and inconsistent processing at 1,600 mm and 3,200 mm digital settings.
Reviews of the display and battery life were positive. PhoneArena measured 3,300 nits of brightness with 20 per cent of the screen illuminated. Android Authority recorded seven to eight hours of active screen use and generally charged the phone every other day. Its stress tests showed thermal throttling during prolonged graphics workloads. Notebookcheck recorded high surface temperatures and reduced sustained performance. Its review rated the display, camera versatility and battery endurance favourably.
Stuff commended general performance, charging and battery life. It identified software clutter and regional availability as the principal obstacles. HardwareZone objected to advertising notifications and folders containing promoted app links in OriginOS on a phone at this price. Android Authority listed the absence of an official United States release and the cost of the optional camera kit among its other reservations.

title: Worlds Collide (September 2026)
text:
The September 2026 Worlds Collide, also promoted as Worlds Collide: Chicago and Los Mundos Chocan (Spanish for "Worlds Collide"), was a professional wrestling livestreaming event and supercard co-produced by the American promotion WWE and its Mexican sister promotion Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide (AAA). It was the sixth Worlds Collide, and the third with AAA, and was held for wrestlers from WWE's Raw, SmackDown, and NXT brand divisions, and those from AAA. It took place on Saturday, September 26, 2026, at the Allstate Arena in the Chicago suburb of Rosemont, Illinois, and aired on tape delay on Wednesday, September 30, on WWE's YouTube channel. It was based around direct competition between wrestlers from the two promotions.
Seven matches were contested at the event. In the main event, SmackDown's CM Punk, Raw wrestler and AAA General Manager Rey Mysterio, and AAA Mega Champion El Grande Americano defeated AAA's Omos and Raw's The Judgment Day (Dominik Mysterio, and JD McDonagh) in a six-man tag team match. In other prominent matches, AAA's La Catalina defeated Raw's Roxanne Perez to retain the AAA Reina de Reinas Championship and AAA's Mini Vikingo defeated SmackDown's Axiom, Raw's Je'Von Evans, and NXT's EK Prosper in a 4-Way, 4-Brand Cruiserweight Contenders match to become the number one contender for the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship.
The event went head-to-head twice against rival American company All Elite Wrestling (AEW). The day the event was taped on September 26, it occurred simultaneously with AEW's pay-per-view event, All Out, which was also held in the Chicago area, and when Worlds Collide was broadcast on September 30, it aired against "A Tribute to Pac", a special episode of the weekly series AEW Dynamite. It also aired against WWE's own Wednesday night program, Evolve.

== Production ==

=== Background ===

Worlds Collide is a series of professional wrestling premium live events (PLE) produced by the American promotion WWE since 2019 and feature direct competition between wrestlers from the promotion's various brands. Following the acquisition of the Mexican promotion Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide (AAA) in 2025, Worlds Collide has since also involved AAA beginning with the June 2025 event.
On July 16, 2026, WWE announced a series of events from late September to early October, including Worlds Collide. The sixth Worlds Collide, and the third with AAA, was scheduled to take place on Saturday, September 26, 2026, at the Allstate Arena in the Chicago suburb of Rosemont, Illinois, with the event also promoted as Los Mundos Chocan (Spanish for "Worlds Collide"). It was held on the same day as All Elite Wrestling (AEW)'s pay-per-view event, All Out, which took place at the nearby Now Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, marking direct WWE–AEW competition in the Chicagoland area. On September 25, WWE announced that the event would not air live and instead, it would air on tape delay on Wednesday, September 30, on WWE's YouTube channel, which put it head-to-head against "A Tribute to Pac", a live special episode of  AEW Dynamite; Pac, who previously wrestled in WWE as Neville from 2012 to 2018, died on September 27, a day after wrestling at All Out.
Chicago native and SmackDown wrestler CM Punk was confirmed to appear at the event. On the September 19 episode of Lucha Libre AAA, AAA General Manager Rey Mysterio revealed the match card and announced that Raw wrestler Oba Femi would appear at Worlds Collide.

=== Storylines ===
The event included seven matches that resulted from scripted storylines. Results were predetermined by writers of the participating promotions, while storylines were produced on WWE's weekly television programs, Raw, SmackDown, NXT, and Lucha Libre AAA, as well as at other WWE and AAA events.
On September 3, AAA announced a fatal four-way match involving Roxanne Perez, Faby Apache, Nattie, and La Hiedra at Night 1 of Triplemanía 34 for the right to challenge for the AAA Reina de Reinas Championship at Worlds Collide. The winner of that match would challenge the winner of the Reina de Reinas Championship match between Flammer and La Catalina at Night 2 of Triplemanía. The number one contender's fatal four-way match at Night 1 of Triplemanía 34 was won by Perez, and at Night 2, Catalina ended Flammer's 1,128-day reign as champion to win the title.

== Event ==

=== Preliminary matches ===
The event opened with the team of AAA's AAA Latin American Champion La Parka, Mr. Iguana, Adelicious, and Mascarita Sagrada versus the team of NXT's The Vanity Project (Brad Baylor, Ricky Smokes, and Myka Lockwood) and AAA's Mini Abismo Negro, accompanied by Jackson Drake. When Lockwood tried to attack Sagrada, Adelicious stopped her before diving to the outside onto Lockwood. Iguana then followed by diving to the outside onto his opponents, which was quickly followed by another dive by Parka. After Sagrada escaped a pinfall attempt by Negro, Sagrada retaliated and then pinned Negro to gain the victory.
The next match was between Raw's Dragon Lee and AAA's Jack Cartwheel. Lee countered a dive by Cartwheel by raising his knees up to make Cartwheel land on his knees. Lee then executed the "Operation Dragon" on Cartwheel, in which Lee backflipped over Cartwheel while grabbing his neck to drive his head backwards down to the mat, before pinning Cartwheel to get the victory.
The third match featured SmackDown's WWE Women's Tag Team Champions Fatal Influence (Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid), accompanied by their leader and WWE Women's United States Champion Jacy Jayne, versus Las Tóxicas (Flammer and AAA World Mixed Tag Team Champion La Hiedra), accompanied by Maravilla. Fatal Influence, along with Jayne, attacked Hiedra in the corner until Hiedra tagged in Flammer. After Flammer dove to the outside onto Fatal Influence, Maravilla and Jayne began to brawl on the outside. Flammer later kicked Reid's jaw, but she was unable to attempt a pinfall because the referee told her that she was not the legal competitor, which confused Flammer. Reid then took advantage of Hiedra's confusion by pinning Hiedra to win the match.
The next match was a 4-Way, 4-Brand Cruiserweight Contenders match to determine the number one contender for the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship, which featured SmackDown's Axiom, NXT's EK Prosper, Raw's Je'Von Evans, and AAA's Mini Vikingo, who later attempted a dive onto Axiom, but Evans interfered by executing a stunner on Vikingo, grabbing Vikingo's head before falling backwards to drive his head down into the mat. Prosper then followed with a moonsault on Evans, in which Prosper performed a backflip off the top rope backwards onto a supine Evans. Vikingo neutralized Prosper by performing a shooting star press on Prosper, jumping off the top rope by performing a backflip onto a supine Prosper. Vikingo then executed a corkscrew 630° splash onto Axiom, in which Vikingo rotated horizontally while performing a double front somersault off the top rope onto a supine Axiom. Vikingo then pinned Axiom to win the match and become the number one contender.
Then, AAA's La Catalina defended the AAA Reina de Reinas Championship against Raw's Roxanne Perez. Early into the match, Perez faked a knee injury to catch Catalina off guard with an attack before revealing her trickery. Perez later illegally put her feet on the ropes for leverage as she attempted a pinfall but the referee caught her. As Perez set Catalina up for an attack, Catalina countered with a backslide pin, in which Catalina hooked Perez's arms after standing back-to-back before kneeling forward to slide Perez backwards onto her shoulders. Catalina then flipped over Perez for leverage to win the match and retain her title.
In the penultimate match, The Lucha Brothers (Raw's Penta and SmackDown and AAA's AAA World Cruiserweight Champion Rey Fénix) faced two-thirds of the AAA World Trios Champions Los Perros del Mal (Daga and Berto), accompanied by AAA World Trios Champion Angel and Karmen Petrovic. As the match progressed, Petrovic interfered by tripping Fénix, allowing Perros del Mal to attack him. Fénix later executed a stunner on Daga, followed by a Mexican Destroyer from Penta on Berto, in which Penta flipped over Berto to force Berto to flip backwards and land his head onto the mat. Daga then attacked Fénix's groin, forcing the referee to end the match and give The Lucha Brothers a win via disqualification. Following the match, Garza entered the ring as Perros del Mal attacked The Lucha Brothers.

=== Main event ===
The main event featured teams consisting of Raw and AAA wrestlers as CM Punk, AAA General Manager Rey Mysterio, and AAA Mega Champion El Grande Americano fought Dominik Mysterio, Omos, and JD McDonagh, accompanied by Dorian Roldán. Rey and Americano executed a clothesline on Omos, in which Rey and Americano used their arms to attack Omos' chest, to send Omos to the outside. Rey then attacked Omos with the "619", in which Rey swung between the ropes to kick Omos' head as Omos rested on the ropes. Punk followed with a dive onto Omos on the outside. Dominik tried to attack Rey with the "619", but Punk blocked him. Punk then executed the "GTS" on McDonagh to win the match via pinfall.
Following the match, Dominik, Omos, and McDonagh attacked Punk, Rey, and Americano. Oba Femi then appeared and went face-to-face with Omos. Femi and Omos began to brawl, which ended when Femi sent Omos to the outside. A furious Omos tried to get back in the ring, but Dominik and McDonagh restrained him and convinced him to retreat.

== Reception ==
WrestleTix reported that WWE and AAA distributed an estimated 13,979 tickets for Worlds Collide.
